jobs.title: Finance Manager, Sales Compensation (Strategic Center of Excellence)
jobs.description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
11 The Role:
The Finance Manager, Sales Compensation (Strategic Center of Excellence) will serve as a strategic and governance advisor, bringing executive presence, strong policy expertise, and a deep understanding of sales compensation strategy. This role will guide the organization through complex business changes while designing legally sound, scalable sales compensation policies.

In addition to core compensation governance, the Finance Manager will oversee all SPIFF and supplemental incentive programs, including KPI collection, validation, and calculation processes to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with business objectives. By applying expertise in sales behavior, incentive design, and SFDC infrastructure, this role will develop effective dispute resolution processes, create engaging training resources, and translate complex compensation methodologies into clear, actionable, and commercially relevant guidance for sales leaders.

Responsibilities and Impact:
This role is the cornerstone of governance, audit compliance, and strategic enablement for our sales compensation operations. By serving as the authoritative voice on policy architecture, managing complex integrations, and ensuring exactness in KPI and SPIFF calculations, the Finance Manager ensures our incentive strategies are seamlessly translated into operational reality, driving both compliance and highly motivated sales behaviors across the organization.
- Establish clear, legally robust, and unambiguous global sales compensation policies. Define global approval matrices and uphold governance standards in partnership with senior Sales, People Partner, and Finance stakeholders.
- Lead the assessment, mapping, and integration of incentive plans and personnel structures during corporate transactions and restructurings. Ensure compensation continuity, policy alignment, and operational readiness during periods of organizational change.
- Manage the end-to-end collection, validation, and calculation of all sales compensation KPIs, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and alignment with plan requirements.
- Oversee and execute calculations for all SPIFFs and custom supplemental incentives, ensuring accuracy, data integrity, and alignment with commercial milestones.
- Analyze and present performance trends, risks, exceptions, and opportunities for process or incentive optimization to senior leadership.
- Manage escalated compensation disputes and define comprehensive dispute-resolution SLAs and policies. Ensure issues are resolved accurately, consistently, and with a customer-centric approach to supporting sales representatives and leaders.
- Evaluate custom supplemental incentives and provide advisory support to commercial and finance stakeholders. Ensure incentive structures are clear, measurable, operationally executable, and aligned with intended sales behaviors.
- Draft step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and governance workflows. Project manage multi-phased initiatives, including the integration of custom incentives, to ensure deliverables remain on track, well-documented, and operationally sustainable.
- Build interactive training libraries for sales representatives and ensure seamless rollout, adoption, and tracking of required compliance and compensation training.

Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates)
S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $ 85,773 to $ 153,091 . Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses and certifications.
In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here .

What We're Looking For:
Basic Required Qualifications:
- 7+ years of relevant experience in sales compensation, finance governance, audit, sales operations, or corporate incentive strategy.
- Governance & Audit Expertise:  Strong background in governance, policy design, internal controls, audit trails, and risk mitigation across complex corporate compensation structures.
- Policy Architecture & Structural Design:  Expert-level capability in writing clear, legally robust, and unambiguous sales compensation policies and terms and conditions.
- KPI, SPIFF & Incentive Calculations:  Hands-on proficiency in collecting, validating, and calculating sales compensation KPIs, SPIFFs, and complex supplemental incentives with high precision.
- Organizational Integration:  Proven track record evaluating, mapping, and integrating incentive plans and personnel structures during corporate transactions, spinoffs, and restructurings.
- Executive Presence & Negotiation:  Ability to uphold governance standards, defend approval matrices, and negotiate policy changes with senior Sales, People Partners, and Finance executives.
- Translational Communication:  Strong ability to translate complex mathematical compensation rules into simple, commercial, and motivating terms for sales representatives and leaders.
- Salesforce/SFDC Proficiency:  Strategic and operational understanding of Salesforce workflows, case queues, routing rules, and dashboard reporting.
- Technical Writing & Digital Enablement:  Expert skill in drafting detailed SOPs, governance workflows, and training materials, and build interactive training libraries and support scalable rollout.
- Customer-Centric Problem Solving & Precision:  Detail-oriented approach to audit compliance, matrix tracking, dispute resolution, and query management, with a supportive and customer-centric mindset.

Right to Work Requirements for US location:
This role is limited to persons with indefinite right to work in the United States.

What’s In It For You?

Our Mission:
Advancing Essential Intelligence.

Our People:
We're more than 35,000 strong worldwide—so we're able to understand nuances while having a broad perspective. Our team is driven by curiosity and a shared belief that Essential Intelligence can help build a more prosperous future for us all.From finding new ways to measure sustainability to analyzing energy transition across the supply chain to building workflow solutions that make it easy to tap into insight and apply it. We are changing the way people see things and empowering them to make an impact on the world we live in. We’re committed to a more equitable future and to helping our customers find new, sustainable ways of doing business. Join us and help create the critical insights that truly make a difference.

Our Values:
Integrity, Discovery, Partnership

Throughout our history, the world's leading organizations have relied on us for the Essential Intelligence they need to make confident decisions about the road ahead. We start with a foundation of integrity in all we do, bring a spirit of discovery to our work, and collaborate in close partnership with each other and our customers to achieve shared goals.

Benefits:
We take care of you, so you can take care of business. We care about our people. That’s why we provide everything you—and your career—need to thrive at S&P Global.

Our benefits include:
- Health & Wellness: Health care coverage designed for the mind and body.

- Flexible Downtime: Generous time off helps keep you energized for your time on.

jobs.title: AI+ Finance Lead
jobs.description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
13
The Role:
S&P Global Inc. is seeking a strategic and innovative AI+ Lead to join our Enterprise Finance and Strategy team. Reporting directly to the Head of Finance AI+ Strategy & Program Management, the AI+ Lead will partner closely with Corporate Finance and divisional CFO’s to implement AI solutions that are scalable, ethical and aligned to corporate objectives for the Finance and Strategy team. This role will work closely with the Head of Finance AI+ Strategy & Program Management to develop the Finance Strategy for AI+ and partner with Finance Leadership Team (FLT) members, Finance Technology Lead, and key AI stakeholders throughout the enterprise to execute the long-term strategy, including artificial intelligence for Finance, automation and robotics. The ideal candidate has prior experience leading initiatives that harness AI/ML, NLP and GenAI technologies to improve Finance processes, operational efficiency and organizational performance.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Planning and Execution:
- Develop and execute a comprehensive AI+ strategy for the Finance team, aligned with SPGI's overall business objectives.

- Identify and prioritize AI opportunities, across Finance processes, including creating a roadmap for AI+ initiatives, outlining key milestones, resources, and timelines.

- Guide the implementation of AI technologies (including automation, robotics, AI/ML, and GenAI), ensuring they integrate smoothly with existing workflows and systems.

- Lead the design and deployment of AI solutions that improve business performance, customer satisfaction and operational efficiencies across the Finance function

Collaboration and Partnership:
- Partner closely with Finance Technology Lead, Corporate Finance, and divisional CFOs to ensure AI solutions are aligned with business needs and stakeholder readiness for AI adoption.

- Facilitate cross-functional collaboration to ensure alignment and buy-in for AI+ initiatives.

- Engage with stakeholders to understand business needs and translate them into AI+ solutions.

- Partner with technology and key stakeholders to influence and shape a data management strategy that supports AI initiatives, focusing on data quality, accessibility and utilization.

Opportunity Discovery and Assessment:
- Conduct readiness assessments with stakeholders to understand their needs, providing through leadership on how AI can drive innovation and solve business problems.

- Evaluate current AI capabilities (data, technology, talent, and processes), identifying gaps and opportunities for improvement.

Implementation Leadership:
- Lead the design and deployment of AI+ projects within the Finance team.

- Coordinate with internal technology teams, Corporate Finance, and external vendors to implement AI+ solutions effectively.

- Articulate the potential of AI/ML, NLP, and GenAI tools, helping stakeholders understand their benefits, limitations, and prerequisites (such as data quality) for successful implementation.

- Monitor project progress, manage risks, and ensure successful delivery of AI+ initiatives.

Metrics and Reporting:
- Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure the success and ROI of AI+ initiatives.

- Prepare and present reports to senior leadership on the progress and outcomes of AI+ projects, highlighting successes, challenges, and areas for optimization

- Develop and implement mechanisms to measure the effectiveness of AI+ strategies and projects, using data analytics to drive continuous improvement

Ethics & Governance:
- Ensure AI initiatives are developed and deployed ethically, following responsible AI practices that address issues such as bias, fairness, and transparency

- Lead the definition of AI governance mechanisms

- Collaborate with internal teams to review AI projects, ensuring they adhere to ethical guidelines and align with regulatory standards.

Thought Leadership:
- Stay abreast of industry trends, emerging technologies, and regulatory developments related to AI, data privacy, and ethics, ensuring compliance.

- Represent the Finance team in internal and external forums related to AI advancements

- Promote a culture of innovation and continuous learning within the team.

Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates)
S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $115,236 to $ 201,357 . Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses and certifications.

In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan.

This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here .

What We’re Looking For:
Basic Required Qualifications:
- 8+ years of experience in finance, digital transformation, or related fields, with substantial experience in implementing AI, automation, or robotics strategies

- Proven experience in leading AI/ML, NLP, and Gen AI projects in a global, complex organizational environment

- Strong project and program management experience, with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders.

- Excellent communication, analytical, and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex concepts into actionable business outcomes

Additional Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience partnering with Finance organizations, including Corporate Finance teams, divisional CFOs, or Finance technology functions.

- Knowledge of AI governance frameworks, responsible AI principles, data privacy regulations, and compliance standards.

- Demonstrated success developing AI roadmaps, establishing adoption strategies, and measuring business impact through KPI and ROI frameworks.

- Passion for innovation with the ability to thrive in ambiguous environments, solve complex business challenges, and drive organizational change.

jobs.title: Director of Public Relations, Chief Technology & Transformation Office
jobs.description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
13 About the Role
S&P Global is seeking a Director of Public Relations to lead external communications for the Chief Technology & Transformation Office (CTTO). This role translates CTTO’s enterprise technology agenda into clear, credible narratives for media, customers, policymakers, partners, and market stakeholders across all technology verticals.

You’ll advise CTTO executives, lead proactive media and executive visibility, and develop communications for major technology milestones, conferences, and awards. You will also support issues management with guidance, messaging materials, and executive preparation in close partnership with the extended Communications and Legal/Policy partners.

Responsibilities
- Lead external technology communications strategy and execution  for CTTO, aligned with Global Technology & Transformation Communications priorities and broader corporate reputation goals.

- Own media relations and spokesperson support  for technology and transformation topics, building relationships with technology, business/financial, and policy reporters.

- Drive AI, data, and transformation storytelling and enablement  by partnering with technology, data, engineering, and transformation leaders to surface proof points, translate complex topics into business value, and identify opportunities to use AI and emerging technologies to enhance communications strategy, execution, workflows, and insights.

- Build executive thought leadership and stakeholder engagement  for CTTO leaders by mapping the network of influential voices they need to engage, developing executive visibility plans, and preparing bylines, Q&As, talking points, interview prep, conference remarks, and social content as needed.

- Provide media training and executive readiness  to ensure CTTO leaders are prepared for priority interviews, external appearances, high-stakes conversations, and ongoing engagement with influential industry, media, policy, and customer voices.

- Manage conferences, speaking, and awards  for priority CTTO moments, including speaker/panel materials and nomination strategy.

- Support issues management  by providing messaging guidance, rapid-response materials, Q&As, and executive readiness for high-scrutiny technology, AI, data, cybersecurity, or policy topics.

- Partner cross-functionally  with Legal, Government Affairs/Policy, Risk/Compliance, Product Marketing, Investor Relations, and business communications to ensure accuracy, consistency, and readiness.

Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates)

S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $126,676 to $221,434 USD. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses and certifications.

In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan.

This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here

What We’re Looking For:

Basic Required Qualifications:
- 10+ years in corporate communications, PR, public affairs, technology communications, policy communications, journalism, or related work.

- Experience leading communications for complex, high-profile technology and policy topics.

- Strong writing/editing skills and ability to distill technical content for senior audiences.

- Proven experience advising executives and preparing leaders for interviews and external appearances.

- Track record building relationships with technology, business/financial, and policy media.

- Strong cross-functional collaboration experience with Legal/Policy/Compliance/Risk stakeholders.

- Proven ability to navigate effectively and efficiently within a large, matrixed global organization while maintaining strong cross-functional alignment and execution discipline.

- Exceptional organization and operational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams in parallel, balance immediate demands with long-term priorities, and operate effectively amid changing requirements, limited resources, and ambiguity.

Additional Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience leading external communications for a global public company, data/AI provider, fintech, cloud/software, or similarly regulated organization.

- Familiarity with AI governance, responsible AI, data regulation, cybersecurity, privacy, and technology risk.

- Experience developing or implementing AI, automation, or emerging technology solutions that improve communications productivity, streamline workflows, or generate actionable insights for decision-making.

- Experience managing conference strategy, speaking, and awards/nominations.

- Existing relationships with top-tier technology and policy reporters.

Success in the First 12 Months
- A clear, repeatable communications operating rhythm for CTTO across media, executive visibility, stakeholder mapping, media training, milestone planning, and disciplined execution of multiple priority workstreams.

- Stronger external visibility and credibility for CTTO leadership across AI, data, transformation, cybersecurity, and policy themes, supported by a clear plan for where executives need to show up and which influential voices they need to engage.

- Consistent, high-quality execution of communications for major CTTO moments, including conferences and awards.

- Effective support for issues management—timely, accurate, and well-prepared messaging and executive readiness.

- Practical use of AI and automation to strengthen communications workflows, improve productivity, and support more data-informed planning and decision-making.

- Improved coordination and trust across CTTO and Communications partner teams.

jobs.title: Reporting & Control Associate / Business Operations & Controls
jobs.description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
10 The Team:

We are a high-performing team dedicated to improving how the organization measures, manages, and reports on operational, risk, and governance activities. Our culture values curiosity, ownership, innovation, and teamwork, empowering individuals to identify opportunities for automation, strengthen governance and control frameworks, enhance reporting capabilities, and drive business process improvements. Team members play a key role in developing governance frameworks, monitoring control effectiveness, producing executive reporting, and delivering insights that support informed decision-making, transparency, operational efficiency, and effective risk management.

Responsibilities and Impact:
Reporting & Scorecard Management
- Support the design, development, maintenance, and enhancement of operational scorecards, dashboards, and management reporting solutions.
- Manage an existing portfolio of business scorecards by monitoring performance, data quality, usage, and stakeholder feedback.
- Partner with business stakeholders to gather requirements and translate business needs into scalable reporting solutions.
- Create executive-level reporting and visualizations that provide actionable insights to senior leadership.

Automation & Data Analytics
- Identify opportunities to automate and improve operational efficiency.
- Develop and maintain Alteryx (Powerautomate) workflows, data pipelines, and automated data preparation processes.
- Leverage Tableau (PowerBI) to create interactive dashboards and visualizations for business users.
- Support integration of data from multiple enterprise systems and platforms.
- Promote an automation-first mindset by identifying scalable solutions that improve data accessibility, consistency, and accuracy.

Governance, Controls & Risk Management
- Assist with the implementation and maintenance of reporting governance standards, data quality controls, and documentation.
- Participate in risk assessments and control reviews to identify potential process improvements.
- Maintain documentation of reporting methodologies, business rules, data sources, and automation workflows.
- Ensure reporting assets comply with established governance, risk, compliance, and data management standards.

- Evaluate new technologies and tools that improve reporting efficiency and analytical capabilities.
- Support process optimization initiatives and implementation of best practices across reporting and controls activities.

Key Competencies
- Data Analytics & Visualization
- Process Automation
- Dashboard & Scorecard Development
- Operational Excellence
- Risk & Control Awareness
- Stakeholder Management
- Problem Solving & Critical Thinking
- Project Coordination
- Communication & Executive Reporting
- Continuous Improvement Mindset

Success Measures
- During the first 12 months, the successful candidate will:
- Successfully manage the existing scorecard portfolio and ensure reporting quality and sustainability.
- Deliver new automated scorecards and reporting enhancements.
- Increase automation of manual reporting processes.
- Improve stakeholder satisfaction and adoption of reporting solutions.
- Contribute to strengthening reporting governance, control, and audit readiness across the organization.
- This position offers a unique opportunity to combine data analytics, automation, reporting, governance, and controls within a highly visible team supporting operational excellence and decision-making across the organization.

What We’re Looking For:

Basic Required Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or related discipline.
- 3-5 years of experience in business operations, reporting, analytics, controls, audit, risk management, governance, or related functions.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data interpretation skills.
- Experience developing and managing operational or management reporting solutions.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities and stakeholders.

Additional Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with Tableau, PowerBI dashboard development.
- Experience with Alteryx workflow or other automation and data transformation tools.
- Experience with Power Automate, Power BI, SQL, Python, or other automation and analytics tools.
- Background in Internal Audit, Operational Risk, Compliance, Controls, Governance, or Regulatory environments.
- Experience supporting audit reviews, remediation programs, control frameworks, or governance initiatives.
- Familiarity with KPI development, scorecard design, and performance measurement frameworks.
- Background in consulting is preferrable
-

jobs.title: Finance Manager, Sales Compensation (Energy)
jobs.description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
11 The Role:
The Finance Manager, Sales Compensation will lead the financial planning, analysis, and operational support of sales incentive programs across the S&P Global Energy business. This role is responsible for helping design and administer compensation plans that motivate sales performance, align to business priorities, and maintain strong financial controls.

This position partners closely with Sales, Sales Operations, People Partners, and Finance leadership to evaluate plan effectiveness, model incentive outcomes, support quota and territory planning, and provide actionable insights on compensation cost, sales productivity, and program performance. The ideal candidate brings a strong blend of financial acumen, analytical rigor, process discipline, and stakeholder management.

Responsibilities and Impact:
This role is central to ensuring the Energy business has compensation programs that are competitive, financially disciplined, and aligned to strategic growth goals. The Finance Manager, Sales Compensation will help shape decisions that influence seller performance, business investment, and overall commercial effectiveness.
- Manage the financial oversight and analysis of sales compensation programs for SPGE, ensuring plans support commercial goals and financial objectives
- Partner with business leaders to design, refine, and evaluate sales incentive plans that drive desired seller behavior and align with growth priorities
- Develop and maintain commission models, incentive calculators, and payout frameworks to support annual planning and in-year program updates
- Support quota setting and territory planning processes by providing financial analysis, scenario modeling, and performance insights
- Forecast sales compensation expense, accruals, and payouts, and provide variance analysis against budget, plan, and prior periods
- Analyze sales performance and compensation outcomes to assess plan effectiveness, cost of sales, pay-for-performance alignment, and return on incentive investment
- Ensure compensation plans, policies, calculations, and payout processes are well documented, controlled, and administered in a manner that supports clean compliance and auditability
- Partner with Sales Operations, People Partners, and Finance teams to ensure compensation plans are clearly documented, operationally executable, and consistently administered
- Review commission calculations and payout processes to ensure accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with plan terms and internal controls
- Identify trends, risks, and opportunities through ongoing analysis of sales results, attainment distributions, payout patterns, and compensation metrics.
- Prepare reporting and presentations for senior leadership on compensation performance, program effectiveness, and financial impact
- Lead or support annual compensation planning cycles, including plan design reviews, modeling, budgeting, and implementation
- Drive process improvements, reporting enhancements, and standardization efforts to improve scalability, transparency, and governance of sales compensation operations
- Support audits, compliance requirements, and policy reviews related to incentive compensation programs

Compensation/Benefits Information: (This section is only applicable to US candidates)
S&P Global states that the anticipated base salary range for this position is $85,773 to $153,091. Final base salary for this role will be based on the individual’s geographic location, as well as experience level, skill set, training, licenses and certifications.
In addition to base compensation, this role is eligible for an annual incentive plan. This role is eligible to receive additional S&P Global benefits. For more information on the benefits we provide to our employees, please click here .

What We're Looking For:
Basic Required Qualifications:
- 7+ years of relevant experience in finance, FP&A, sales compensation, sales operations, or incentive planning, with demonstrated progression in scope and responsibility
- Strong understanding of sales compensation principles, including incentive plan design, commissions, quota methodologies, territory setting and payout governance
- Proven experience in financial modeling, forecasting, budgeting, and performance analysis
- Ability to translate complex data into clear business insights and practical recommendations for leadership
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with high attention to detail and accuracy
- Experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders, including commercial leaders, HR, Finance, and Sales Operations
- Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience working with compensation, planning, or reporting systems
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and build credibility across functions
- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment
